description.value: A longitudinal 18F-FDG PET study examining progression of cerebral glucose metabolism in patients with mild frontotemporal dementia.

spans.text: The aim of this study was to determine the progression of changes in cerebral glucose metabolism in FTD in a follow-up study using 18F-fluoro-2-desoxy- d -glucose positron emission tomography scanning (18F-FDG-PET)

value: At follow-up, patients with FTD showed a significant further decrease of glucose metabolism relative to baseline in all cortical areas where hypometabolism had been observed at the initial examination.

Significant reductions were also observed in regions unaffected at baseline, including the inferior frontal cortex, inferior parietal lobe, left precuneus, and inferior and middle temporal lobes bilaterally.
These findings indicate that during disease progression the pathological changes surpass the borders of the frontal lobe and spread into the parietal and temporal cortices.
The magnitude of the decline could not be indicated because absolute quantitation was not used in the FDG measurements.

spans.text: Analysis of cerebral metabolic decline in patients with FTD as a group at follow-up showed a significant further decrease of glucose metabolism relative to baseline in all cortical areas where hypometabolism had been observed at the initial examination. In addition, significant reductions in glucose metabolism were also observed in brain regions that were unaffected at baseline, including the inferior frontal cortex, the inferior parietal lobe, and, to a lesser extent, the inferior and the middle temporal lobe bilaterally (pFDRcorr < 0.05) ( ).
